---
title: "greta#855 (tf-warmup-i547): effective samples from its warmup tuning"
description: "Effective samples per sampler iteration and per second of `mcmc()` with each version's defaults on main and greta#855, on four of greta's examples over twenty sessions. #855's warmup tunes to larger step sizes, gives more effective samples per sampler iteration on three of the four models, and gives 2.8 to 7.9 times main's effective samples per second."
date: 2026-10-13
bibliography: ../../references.bib
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| code-summary: "Setup"
source(here::here("posts", "_helpers.R"))

post_path <- "posts/2026-10-13-tuning-efficiency-i547"
file_link <- file_linker(post_path)
section_link <- section_linker(post_path)
# the sections of benchmark.R, shown below by their labels
knitr::read_chunk(here(post_path, "benchmark.R"))

sessions <- read_sessions(post_path)
n_sessions <- length(sessions)

version_labels <- c(main = "main", `#855` = "#855")
versions <- display_versions(sessions[[1]]$versions, labels = version_labels)
version_levels <- names(versions)
colours <- version_colours(version_levels)
settings <- sessions[[1]]$results[[1]]$settings

# how the text names each version: main links to its commit, #855 to the PR
version_text <- c(
  main = paste0("[main](", commit_url(versions[["main"]]), ")"),
  `#855` = paste0("[#855](", pr_url(855), ")")
)
version_ref <- function(version) I(version_text[[version]])

# one row per session and version, holding that version's results
runs <- lapply(sessions, function(session_file) {
  tibble(
    session = session_file$session,
    version = factor(
      unname(version_labels[names(session_file$results)]),
      levels = version_levels
    ),
    results = unname(session_file$results)
  )
}) |>
  bind_rows()

model_levels <- names(runs$results[[1]]$mcmc)
# benchmark.R's section for each model
model_sections <- paste0("mcmc-", gsub("_", "-", model_levels))

# one row per run of mcmc(): its timed calls, the last call's draws, the
# sampler iterations each draw cost, and what warmup tuned hmc() to
mcmc_runs <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(runs)), function(i) {
  results <- runs$results[[i]]
  lapply(model_levels, function(model_name) {
    run <- results$mcmc[[model_name]]
    tibble(
      session = runs$session[i],
      version = runs$version[i],
      model = model_name,
      call_seconds = list(as.numeric(run$marks$time[[1]])),
      draws = list(run$draws),
      iterations_per_draw = results$sampler_iterations_per_draw,
      epsilon = run$epsilon,
      diag_sd = list(run$diag_sd)
    )
  }) |>
    bind_rows()
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = model_levels))

# small dots for the sessions over a large faint dot for their mean
gg_sessions <- function(data, means, measure, x_label) {
  ggplot(data, aes(x = {{ measure }}, y = version, colour = version)) +
    geom_point(data = means, size = 5, alpha = 0.25) +
    geom_point(
      position = position_jitter(width = 0, height = 0.2, seed = 2026),
      size = 1.2
    ) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = colours, guide = "none") +
    facet_wrap(vars(model), ncol = 2, scales = "free_x") +
    labs(x = x_label, y = NULL)
}
session_caption <- "Each small dot is one session's run. The large faint dot behind them is the mean of the sessions."

# what each "Run it yourself" block runs: setup, the iteration count, and every
# model
run_code <- run_it_yourself(
  post_path,
  "benchmark.R",
  c("setup", "sampler-iterations", model_sections),
  versions,
  paste0(
    "list(sampler_iterations_per_draw = sampler_iterations_per_draw, ",
    paste0(model_levels, " = mcmc_", model_levels, collapse = ", "),
    ")"
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| label: efficiency
#| code-summary: "The measures, and each version's mean"
# posterior caps a bulk ESS at S × log10(S) for S draws, which anticorrelated
# draws can reach, and warns each time. The warnings are counted here and
# reported under Convergence
ess_cap_warnings <- 0
summarise_counting_caps <- function(draws) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    posterior::summarise_draws(draws, "mean", "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail"),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("The ESS has been capped", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        ess_cap_warnings <<- ess_cap_warnings + 1
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}

# everything is from the run's last call, whose draws were kept
efficiency <- mcmc_runs |>
  mutate(
    posterior = lapply(draws, summarise_counting_caps),
    n_draws = vapply(draws, posterior::ndraws, numeric(1)),
    seconds = vapply(
      call_seconds,
      \(times) times[[settings$mcmc_calls]],
      numeric(1)
    ),
    smallest_ess_bulk = vapply(posterior, \(summary) min(summary$ess_bulk), numeric(1)),
    smallest_ess_tail = vapply(posterior, \(summary) min(summary$ess_tail), numeric(1)),
    largest_rhat = vapply(posterior, \(summary) max(summary$rhat), numeric(1)),
    smallest_ess_capped = smallest_ess_bulk >=
      n_draws * log10(n_draws) * (1 - 1e-9),
    sampler_iterations = n_draws * iterations_per_draw,
    ess_per_iteration = smallest_ess_bulk / sampler_iterations,
    ess_per_second = smallest_ess_bulk / seconds
  ) |>
  select(-call_seconds, -draws, -diag_sd, -posterior)

# each version's mean over the sessions, for each model
efficiency_means <- efficiency |>
  group_by(model, version) |>
  summarise(
    across(c(epsilon, ess_per_iteration, ess_per_second), mean),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# #855's mean over main's, for each model
pr_over_main <- efficiency_means |>
  pivot_longer(
    c(epsilon, ess_per_iteration, ess_per_second),
    names_to = "measure"
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = version, values_from = value) |>
  mutate(ratio = `#855` / main)
ratio_of <- function(measure_name, model_name) {
  pr_over_main$ratio[
    pr_over_main$measure == measure_name & pr_over_main$model == model_name
  ]
}

# "#855 gives 1.4 times main's", for one measure and model
compare_on <- function(measure_name, model_name) {
  compare_rates(
    ratio_of(measure_name, model_name),
    version_text[["#855"]],
    version_text[["main"]]
  )
}
```

[greta#855](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/pull/855) runs `hmc()`'s warmup inside TensorFlow, and its warmup tunes the step size to different values from main's. This post runs `{r} version_ref("main")` and `{r} version_ref("#855")` with each version's defaults on four of greta's examples, in `{r} n_sessions` sessions, to see whether that changes how many effective samples `mcmc()` gives. Taking the smallest bulk ESS of each run, and each version's mean over the sessions, per sampler iteration (which leaves out how fast the code runs) and per second:

- linear:
    - per sampler iteration, `{r} compare_on("ess_per_iteration", "linear")`
    - per second, `{r} compare_on("ess_per_second", "linear")`
- multiple_linear:
    - per sampler iteration, `{r} compare_on("ess_per_iteration", "multiple_linear")`
    - per second, `{r} compare_on("ess_per_second", "multiple_linear")`
- hierarchical_linear:
    - per sampler iteration, `{r} compare_on("ess_per_iteration", "hierarchical_linear")`
    - per second, `{r} compare_on("ess_per_second", "hierarchical_linear")`
- eight_schools:
    - per sampler iteration, `{r} compare_on("ess_per_iteration", "eight_schools")`
    - per second, `{r} compare_on("ess_per_second", "eight_schools")`

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## How it was tested

**The versions.**

- **`{r} version_ref("main")`**: `{r} I(version_link(versions[["main"]]))`. Each draw costs `thin + 1` sampler iterations, two at the default `thin = 1`, and each warmup step runs the same way, so its defaults of `warmup = 1000` and `n_samples = 1000` run 2000 iterations in each phase. It tunes `epsilon` and `diag_sd` in R between bursts of three warmup steps, and draws `hmc()`'s number of leapfrog steps once per burst.
- **`{r} version_ref("#855")`**: `{r} I(version_link(versions[["#855"]]))`. Each draw and each warmup step is one sampler iteration, and its defaults of `warmup = 2000` and `n_samples = 2000` run the same 2000 iterations in each phase as main's. It tunes inside TensorFlow every three iterations, on the same schedule as main: `epsilon` by dual averaging [@hoffman2014] over the first 10% and last 60% of warmup, `diag_sd` between 10% and 40%. It draws the number of leapfrog steps afresh every iteration.

**The models**, four of greta's examples. Normal and log-normal distributions are written with their mean and standard deviation, as greta's `normal()` and `lognormal()` take them; $\text{Cauchy}^{+}$ is a Cauchy truncated to positive values.

::: panel-tabset

#### linear

Each department's rating in `attitude` regressed on its number of complaints.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{rating}_i &\sim \text{Normal}(\mu_i, \sigma), \quad i = 1, \dots, 30 \\
\mu_i &= \alpha + \beta \, \text{complaints}_i \\
\alpha, \beta &\sim \text{Normal}(0, 10) \\
\sigma &\sim \text{Cauchy}^{+}(0, 3)
\end{aligned}
$$

```{r}
#| label: mcmc-linear
#| eval: false
#| code-summary: "benchmark.R: mcmc-linear"
```

#### multiple_linear

The same rating on all six of `attitude`'s other columns, $X$, through a matrix multiply.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{rating}_i &\sim \text{Normal}(\mu_i, \sigma), \quad i = 1, \dots, 30 \\
\mu_i &= \alpha + \sum_{j = 1}^{6} X_{ij} \, \beta_j \\
\alpha, \beta_j &\sim \text{Normal}(0, 10) \\
\sigma &\sim \text{Cauchy}^{+}(0, 3)
\end{aligned}
$$

```{r}
#| label: mcmc-multiple-linear
#| eval: false
#| code-summary: "benchmark.R: mcmc-multiple-linear"
```

#### hierarchical_linear

Sepal length on sepal width in `iris`, with an offset for each species, $s[i]$ being flower $i$'s. Setosa's offset is zero and the other two share a scale, $\tau$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Sepal.Length}_i &\sim \text{Normal}(\mu_i, \sigma), \quad i = 1, \dots, 150 \\
\mu_i &= \alpha + \beta \, \text{Sepal.Width}_i + \gamma_{s[i]} \\
\gamma_1 &= 0, \qquad \gamma_2, \gamma_3 \sim \text{Normal}(0, \tau) \\
\tau &\sim \text{LogNormal}(0, 1) \\
\alpha, \beta &\sim \text{Normal}(0, 10) \\
\sigma &\sim \text{Cauchy}^{+}(0, 3)
\end{aligned}
$$

```{r}
#| label: mcmc-hierarchical-linear
#| eval: false
#| code-summary: "benchmark.R: mcmc-hierarchical-linear"
```

#### eight_schools

The effect of coaching in eight schools, $y_j$, each measured with a known standard error, $\sigma_j$. The scale of the school effects, $\sigma_\eta$, is itself a parameter, which makes the posterior a funnel.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y_j &\sim \text{Normal}(\theta_j, \sigma_j), \quad j = 1, \dots, 8 \\
\theta_j &= \mu + \xi \, \eta_j \\
\eta_j &\sim \text{Normal}(0, \sigma_\eta) \\
\sigma_\eta &\sim \text{InverseGamma}(1, 1) \\
\mu &\sim \text{Normal}(0, 100) \\
\xi &\sim \text{Normal}(0, 5)
\end{aligned}
$$

```{r}
#| label: mcmc-eight-schools
#| eval: false
#| code-summary: "benchmark.R: mcmc-eight-schools"
```

:::

**What was run.** In each session, each version ran `mcmc()` with `{r} settings$chains` chains, `verbose = FALSE`, the default sampler, `hmc()`, and its own default `warmup` and `n_samples` on each model, calling it `{r} settings$mcmc_calls` times on the model, the first call tracing it. Everything here is from the last call: its runtime, its draws, and the `epsilon` and `diag_sd` warmup tuned, read from the result (`time_mcmc()`, in the `{r} section_link("benchmark.R", "setup")` section).

**What was measured.** The bulk effective sample size (ESS) [@vehtari2021] of each run's worst-mixing parameter, as @hoffman2014 report it:

- per sampler iteration of the sampling phase: the draws, times the sampler iterations each draw costs, which the `{r} section_link("benchmark.R", "sampler-iterations")` section counts with a random walk. Both versions draw the number of leapfrog steps uniformly from 5 to 10, so this is in proportion to ESS per gradient evaluation. It is what the tuning gives, apart from how fast the code runs.
- per second of the call, warmup included: the time-normalised ESS of @girolami2011, which is what a user gets.

**The sessions.** `{r} file_link("run.R")` installed each version as its `{r} section_link("run.R", "run-versions")` section says, and ran `{r} file_link("benchmark.R")` for each in a fresh R session of its own, in `{r} n_sessions` sessions, the order rotating so that each version ran first equally often (its `{r} section_link("run.R", "run-sessions")` section). Each session gives each version one seed, `session_seed`. Every version ran on TensorFlow `{r} runs$results[[1]]$provenance$tensorflow_version`, TensorFlow Probability `{r} runs$results[[1]]$provenance$tfp_version` and reticulate `{r} runs$results[[1]]$provenance$reticulate_version`, on `{r} runs$results[[1]]$provenance$machine` with `{r} runs$results[[1]]$provenance$cores` cores.

## Step size warmup tunes to {#step-size}

`epsilon`, the step size `hmc()` takes after warmup, in each run. Each parameter's step is `epsilon` times its `diag_sd` over the sum of `diag_sd`, so `epsilon` is the sum of the parameters' steps.

```{r}
#| label: plot-epsilon
#| fig-cap: !expr session_caption
gg_sessions(efficiency, efficiency_means, epsilon, "epsilon")
```

`{r} timed_by(section_link, "benchmark.R", c("setup", model_sections), verb = "Tuned")`

```{r}
#| label: run-epsilon
#| eval: false
#| code-summary: "Run it yourself"
#| code: !expr run_code
```

```{r}
#| label: epsilon-words
# "#855's is 1.2 to 1.5 times main's" over the models, naming the version
# with the larger mean epsilon
epsilon_ratios <- pr_over_main$ratio[pr_over_main$measure == "epsilon"]
pr_epsilon <- paste0(version_text[["#855"]], "'s")
main_epsilon <- paste0(version_text[["main"]], "'s")
larger_epsilon <- if (all(epsilon_ratios >= 1)) {
  paste(pr_epsilon, "is", format_range(epsilon_ratios), "times", main_epsilon)
} else if (all(epsilon_ratios <= 1)) {
  paste(main_epsilon, "is", format_range(1 / epsilon_ratios), "times", pr_epsilon)
} else {
  paste0(
    "it varies: ",
    pr_epsilon,
    " is up to ",
    format_number(max(epsilon_ratios)),
    " times ",
    main_epsilon,
    ", and ",
    main_epsilon,
    " up to ",
    format_number(max(1 / epsilon_ratios)),
    " times ",
    pr_epsilon
  )
}
```

Over the four models, `{r} I(larger_epsilon)`.

<details><summary>Figure: each parameter's step</summary>

```{r}
#| label: plot-steps
#| fig-height: 8
steps <- mcmc_runs |>
  mutate(
    step = Map(
      \(epsilon, diag_sd) epsilon * diag_sd / sum(diag_sd),
      epsilon,
      diag_sd
    )
  ) |>
  select(session, version, model, step) |>
  mutate(parameter = lapply(step, seq_along)) |>
  unnest(c(step, parameter)) |>
  # each version's dots a little above or below their parameter's line
  mutate(row = parameter + ifelse(version == "main", 0.15, -0.15))

ggplot(steps, aes(x = step, y = row, colour = version)) +
  geom_point(size = 1, alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = \(limits) seq(1, floor(limits[2]))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colours) +
  facet_wrap(vars(model), ncol = 2, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Step (log scale)", y = "Free parameter", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

Each dot is one session's run. The free parameters are numbered in the order greta keeps them, on the scale `hmc()` samples them on.

</details>

## Does every run converge? {#convergence}

The largest R-hat [@vehtari2021] of each run, over its parameters. Above 1.01, the chains have not mixed well enough for their ESS to be trusted.

```{r}
#| label: plot-rhat
#| fig-cap: "Each small dot is one session's run. The dashed line is at 1.01."
ggplot(efficiency, aes(x = largest_rhat, y = version, colour = version)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1.01, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(
    position = position_jitter(width = 0, height = 0.2, seed = 2026),
    size = 1.2
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colours, guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(vars(model), ncol = 2, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Largest R-hat", y = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: convergence
# for each model and version, the median run's largest R-hat, the highest, and
# how many runs are above 1.01
convergence <- efficiency |>
  group_by(model, version) |>
  summarise(
    `median largest R-hat` = median(largest_rhat),
    `highest` = max(largest_rhat),
    `runs above 1.01` = paste(sum(largest_rhat > 1.01), "of", n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
capped <- efficiency |> filter(smallest_ess_capped)
knitr::kable(convergence, digits = 3)
```

With `{r} settings$chains` chains of `{r} format_number(unique(efficiency$sampler_iterations) / settings$chains)` sampler iterations, the median run's largest R-hat is `{r} format_range(convergence[["median largest R-hat"]])` over the models and versions, and the highest is `{r} format_number(max(efficiency$largest_rhat))`, so one run's smallest ESS is a rough estimate. The posterior package capped `{r} ess_cap_warnings` ESS estimates at S × log10(S) for S draws, which anticorrelated draws reach, and `{r} nrow(capped)` runs had a capped estimate as their smallest bulk ESS.
